claims.claim: SQM's 2025 annual filing describes an approximately US$2.7 billion 2025-2027 capital-expenditure program focused mainly on production-capacity expansion, including Chile lithium capacity, a seawater pipeline, iodine capacity and Australian lithium projects; this creates a source-addressed capital-intensity and execution-risk channel that Alpha can incorporate without Beta assigning a numeric risk score.
causalEdges: multi-year expansion capex -> funding/cash deployment -> future capacity and resilience
claims.risk: Large multi-year capital commitments can reduce resilience if commodity economics weaken or projects experience cost/schedule slippage.
claims.falsifier: On-budget/on-schedule execution, sustained liquidity and demand absorption with competitive unit economics would weaken this risk.

claims.claim: The same annual filing reports dividends paid fell sharply from US$1.5 billion in 2023 to US$67.2 million in 2024 and US$4.3 million in 2025, explicitly linking the reduction to lower net income associated with lower lithium prices; this is direct evidence that lithium-price cyclicality transmits into shareholder distributions and financial flexibility.
causalEdges: lithium price decline -> lower net income -> lower distributions
commodity clearing price -> cash generation -> capital-allocation flexibility
claims.risk: Current strong lithium-period earnings should not be assumed to represent normalized cash generation through the cycle.
claims.falsifier: Durable cash generation and distributions through materially weaker lithium pricing would demonstrate stronger cycle resilience than this historical transmission suggests.

risks: multi-year capital intensity and project execution risk
commodity-price cyclicality transmitting into earnings and distributions
unknowns: Future realized project returns, schedule adherence and funding mix are not established by the annual filing alone.
This evidence does not establish Alpha's numeric risk magnitude or score.
recommendedNextState: council-alpha should consume the primary-source risk channels when constructing source-addressed score-risk evidence and retain numeric underwriting authority

doctrine.observedWeakness: capital intensity and commodity-linked earnings/distribution sensitivity
doctrine.uncertainty: future project economics and cycle durability
doctrine.possibleImprovement: demonstrated project execution, liquidity resilience and lower-cost capacity through the cycle
doctrine.evidenceNeeded: subsequent capex delivery, unit-cost, liquidity, leverage and cycle cash-generation evidence
